the use of trees of paths in the core of the network is a good alternative to MPLS tunnels and that the use of off-the-shelf equipments and protocols is possible to achieve this goal.
we propose a new approach for traffic engineering in core networks that relies on the use of a logically centralized controller and on the implementation of simple routing algorithms in the core.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and evaluation of a novel network architecture that is able to support traffic engineering goals in a scalable manner.
designing and evaluating a new architecture to support the dynamic adaptation of load balancing in backbone networks.
the design of algorithms for the selection of paths and their aggregation, and the implementation of these algorithms in a network using off-the-shelf routers and protocols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we show that a logically centralized controller may use a priori computed and statically configured paths in the core of the network to implement load balancing and network resilience.
the proposed solution is able to achieve the same goals as the state of the art, with much less complexity in the core of the network.
our algorithms and protocols are a first step towards a simpler core network, that can be built using off-the-shelf equipments, and that can be controlled by a logically centralized software.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it is possible to achieve traffic engineering goals with a simple approach, where the network core only implements many a-priori computed paths, while the edge of the net- work adapts the load balancing to current needs and network status.

the core of a network can be simplified by using only simple protocols and their most common implementation, and that the edge of the net- work can be made to adapt to traffic engineering goals by using a logically central- ized controller that uses a priori selected paths.
it is possible to implement a simple and efficient traffic engineering solution using only a small amount of off-the-shelf equipments and protocols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and cost-effective solution to traffic engineering is within reach.
a simple and cheap network can be built using off-the-shelf hardware and protocols, but with the same traffic engineering goals as current networks.

the same traffic engineering goals can be achieved with a simpler approach, that only requires a logically centralized controller, that can be implemented with off-the-shelve equipment and protocols, and that does not require expensive and sophisticated equipments in the core.
